text: [Loyola Marymount Univ. v. Hartford Acc. & Indem. Co. (1990) 219 CA3d 1217, 1225, 271 CR 528, 532] b. [3:469] “Personal injury liability” coverage? Employment discrimination claims do not fit within any of the “offenses” enumerated in the separate CGL coverage for “personal injury liability” (e.g., defamation, false imprisonment, malicious prosecution, etc.; see ¶ 3:298). However, nonstandard policies may define “personal injury” more broadly: (1) [3:470] (Nonstandard) definition including “humiliation”: Some liability policies define “personal injury” to include injury arising out of “libel, slander, defamation of character, humiliation or invasion of privacy …” “Humiliation” by itself is not an actionable tort but, rather, a form of damages (emotional distress). Therefore, there is no 9 “personal injury” coverage for “humiliation” damages resulting from noncovered risks; e.g., employment discrimination. [American Motorists Ins. Co. v.
